content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3 (full recovery with overtime): best policy-compliant plan, lifting service level to 75.9% for 10:45-14:45, still short of the 80% target, for Rs 11,397.","why":"Payments handle time has climbed from about 296 s to 556 s, most likely because of system slowness (ticket INC-20261118-1085, 30-60 s saves on chargeback/dispute screens). Volume is only modestly up. With no action, service level over 10:45-14:45 is predicted at 57.9%, with payments at 46.5% and abandons at 11.4%. P3 combines break delays, IVR callback, 20% chat deflection, overtime offers (40 agents 11:15-13:15, 5 agents 13:15-15:15) and cancelling the 15:30 coaching. That gives 75.9% overall (payments 74.6%, general 77.7%), cuts abandons to 5.6%, and lifts the rest of day to 84.1%. No plan within policy reaches 80%, so this is the best available.","trade_offs":["P4 costs about the same (Rs 11,292) and is close (75.6%, abandons 5.9%). It uses no IVR callback, so customer impact is lower, but it relies on 50 overtime takers in one block and does slightly worse on payments (73.6%).","R1 (85.0%) and R2 (83.6%) would hit the 80% target, but both break the Rs 15,000 overtime budget (expected Rs 17,568 and Rs 17,280), so they are not allowed under policy.","The no-cost options P1 (54.7%) and P2 (58.2%, Rs 1,317) barely move service level. P1 is actually worse than doing nothing.","P3 asks customers to accept callbacks and agents to accept delayed breaks. In return, general queue holds at 77.7%, better than with no action (72.3%), so there is no risk to the other queue."],"watch":"Track overtime uptake for the 11:15 block. If far fewer than 40 agents accept, payments will fall well short of 74.6%. Push for the system ticket fix: if handle time recovers, release the overtime early. If it keeps rising, the plan will underdeliver and you should involve the duty manager about the budget."}
